meta.intro: These Blox Fruits tier rankings reflect awakened forms in the current meta and are refreshed weekly. New players still deciding their first purchase should start with the basics on the [Blox Fruits hub](/blox-fruits) and the step-by-step [redeem guide](/blox-fruits/redeem-guide) before committing Beli or Robux — the meta picks here are not the same as the easiest picks to level with. If you're not sure which fruit fits your playstyle, the [Fruit Decision Helper](/blox-fruits/which-fruit) walks you through four questions and recommends the top three matches. The 25 fruits below cover every Common through Mythical that's still relevant in the current patch; freshly added or pre-rework removals are omitted. Tier calls here are editorial and judged from current upstream wiki consensus plus our own play-testing notes, refreshed every Sunday. For freshly added in-game promos that pair well with whichever fruit you pick, see the [latest working codes](/blox-fruits/latest) — XP boosts are particularly worth stacking when you're grinding a new Mythical.

fruits.name: Dragon
fruits.oneLineReason: Meta-defining PvP and grinding kit; nothing else is close.
fruits.tierRationale: Dragon is the current meta-defining pick. Awakened form gives you full-screen air-pressure zoning, a transformation that doubles your survivability, and combo-extenders that close out PvP fights from neutral. Grinding is also class-leading thanks to the AOE pressure scaling with level.
pros: Awakened transformation is the strongest defensive layer in the game right now
Air-pressure zoning denies space at a range no other fruit matches
Top-tier in all three dimensions — rare even among Mythicals
cons: Highest Robux cost of any fruit; Beli grind is also brutal
Awakening fragment cost is steep — expect multiple raid cycles
Skill ceiling is high; new owners often underperform B-tier picks until ~50 hours in

bestCombos.notes: Pair with Ghoul or Shark race for sustained pressure; Cyborg race is also strong for the energy regen.

fruits.name: Leopard
fruits.oneLineReason: Best combo-extender in the game; PvP king if you can land it.
fruits.tierRationale: Classic PvP king. The fastest combo-extender in the game lets you chain Z and X almost indefinitely with the right race. Grinding drops slightly behind Dragon and Buddha because the AOE is smaller, but combo damage on bosses is still top-tier.
pros: Single best combo-extender — TKO and TKO follow-ups are nearly unblockable
Movement speed buff in transformation makes catching runners trivial
Holds value in trading even years after release
cons: Awakening adds less than most Mythicals — the base form is already most of the value
Bossing relies on staying close, which Dragon avoids
Counter-picked hard by Spirit and Venom in 1v1 trades

bestCombos.notes: Ghoul race nearly required for the lifesteal — Leopard's only weakness is sustain in long trades.

howToObtain: Trading — typically valued just under Dragon

fruits.name: Dough
fruits.oneLineReason: Awakened AOE traps; second-best PvP fruit at a lower Robux floor.
fruits.tierRationale: Awakened Dough sits a hair below Dragon in PvP — the AOE on the Z move and the size of the V trap give it the second-best zoning kit. Grinding is decent thanks to the wide hitboxes, but cooldowns lag behind Buddha and Dragon for sustained farming.
pros: Awakening completely transforms the kit — pre-awakening Dough is mid-tier, awakened is meta
Massive AOE traps make group fights and sea events trivial
Lower Robux cost than Dragon or Leopard for similar PvP performance
cons: Pre-awakening it's a B-tier fruit, which means a long fragment grind before payoff
Cooldowns on the strong moves are long — windows of vulnerability after every commitment
Less popular in trading than other Mythicals

bestCombos.notes: Mink race for the speed makes landing the awakened V trap consistent.

fruits.name: Buddha
fruits.oneLineReason: Cheapest fast path to clean grinding; tank everything, no combos needed.
fruits.tierRationale: The grinding workhorse. Transformation gives you huge hitboxes, M1 lifesteal scaling, and damage reduction — three reasons Buddha clears mob farms and bossing faster than any other fruit. PvP is solid but not top-tier; the slow moves get out-spaced by Dragon and Dough.
pros: Cheapest path to clean grinding at high levels — saves real Beli grind
Damage reduction in transformation lets you tank hits that would one-shot other fruits
Easy to use — minimal skill expression needed to be effective
cons: PvP ceiling is capped — hard-countered by any zoning fruit
Single-target boss damage isn't class-leading despite the lifesteal
Looks visually unimpressive, which matters for trading liquidity

bestCombos.notes: Shark race for the underwater grinding bonus; Cyborg also great for the extra health.

howToObtain: Blox Fruit Dealer (Legendary roll, common compared to Mythicals)

fruits.name: Spirit
fruits.oneLineReason: Summon + spectral kit; PvP only — grinding will hurt.
fruits.tierRationale: A genuine PvP terror — summon mechanics let you fight with effective two-vs-one numbers, and the spectral form ignores most projectile damage. The catch is grinding: the kit has zero AOE, so mob clears are painful. Pick Spirit only if you're a PvP main.
pros: Summon mechanic gives a real numerical advantage in 1v1s
Spectral mode is the most unique defensive layer in the game
Niche but devoted following — trading liquidity holds up
cons: Grinding is the worst of any Mythical — D-tier for a reason
Heavy keybind dependence; not pick-up-and-play
Awakening adds quality-of-life but doesn't fix the grinding problem

bestCombos.notes: Ghoul race for sustain; Spirit's defense pairs uniquely well with lifesteal.

fruits.name: Venom
fruits.oneLineReason: Damage-over-time forces commitment; high-floor all-rounder.
fruits.tierRationale: Poison damage-over-time makes Venom consistent — you can land a tick from neutral and force the opponent to commit. Awakening adds toxic AOE that makes the kit a strong all-rounder. The ceiling is lower than Dragon or Dough, but the floor is much higher.
pros: DoT removes the need to commit to risky combo openers
Toxic AOE makes group PvP and Castle of Sea Beasts trivial
Forgiving for intermediate players — high floor, moderate ceiling
cons: Outclassed at the top end by Dragon, Leopard, and Dough
Awakening is required to be competitive — long fragment grind
Trading value lags behind despite the strength

bestCombos.notes: Ghoul or Cyborg race; both reinforce the attrition playstyle.

fruits.name: Shadow
fruits.oneLineReason: Safe-pick generalist; A everywhere, S nowhere.
fruits.tierRationale: The textbook generalist — no extremes in any direction. Awakened Shadow has solid AOE for grinding, a passive damage buff during night-time, and a teleport that's serviceable for combo extension. If you're new to the Mythical tier and unsure what playstyle you want, Shadow is the safest pick.
pros: All three dimensions are A-tier — no glaring weakness
Night-time damage passive is a free bonus most fruits don't get
Teleport opens up combo routes that other fruits can't access
cons: Never the best at anything — outpicked by specialists in every category
Night-only passive means daytime fights lose value
Visual effects are subtle, hurting trading appeal

bestCombos.notes: Mink race amplifies the mobility theme; works with most races though.

fruits.name: Gravity
fruits.oneLineReason: Orbital-pull AOE; reliable PvP at a Legendary price point.
fruits.tierRationale: Gravity rewards positioning more than reaction speed. The pull-in on Z and the meteor on X give you a complete neutral game without needing combos. Grinding works once you learn the cast timing, but it's slower than Beast fruits and the AOE shape favors clusters of enemies, not spread mobs.
pros: One of the few Legendary fruits that genuinely competes with Mythicals in 1v1
Pull-in setups are reliable openers for any sword you bring
Cheaper Robux barrier than Mythical PvP fruits with similar payoff
cons: Cast animations are long — punished hard by Light or Rumble speed
Grinding scales poorly on spread enemy spawns
No awakening, so the ceiling caps below Mythical zoners

bestCombos.notes: Mink race covers the slow cast windows; Ghoul also viable for sustain.

fruits.name: Rumble
fruits.oneLineReason: Long-range bolts and a strong escape; reliable Legendary PvP.
fruits.tierRationale: Lightning coverage with reliable hitboxes — Rumble is the textbook 'second fruit' for accounts that already have a grinder. PvP is genuinely good thanks to the long-range bolt and a strong escape on F. Grinding falls behind because the AOE doesn't scale as well as Beast fruits.
pros: One of the most reliable PvP picks at the Legendary price point
Long-range coverage means you can pressure runners and runners can't escape
Awakening cost is moderate — accessible upgrade path
cons: Grinding falls off in late-game farms
Counter-picked by Sand and Light (light wins the speed war)
Less trading value than equivalent-tier Beast fruits

bestCombos.notes: Mink race doubles the speed identity; great for chase-down playstyle.

fruits.name: Quake
fruits.oneLineReason: Shockwave AOE; classic mid-game grinder with PvP upside.
fruits.tierRationale: Quake's shockwaves are some of the best AOE in the Legendary bracket — wide hitboxes, decent damage, and uppercut combo openers. PvP is functional but not exceptional; once people learn to dodge the linear shockwave it loses bite. Solid mid-game pick between Light and a Mythical.
pros: Strong AOE for mob clears at Sea 2 and early Sea 3 levels
Uppercut on F is one of the better combo-starters at this tier
Holds value in trading among newer players who skip Light
cons: Linear hitboxes are dodged easily by experienced players
Falls off hard once you can access Mythical fruits
Awakening only adds incremental value — not a fruit you keep long-term

bestCombos.notes: Any race works; Mink for movement, Cyborg for survivability.

fruits.name: Magma
fruits.oneLineReason: Burn DoT plus wide AOE; the budget pre-Mythical grinder.
fruits.tierRationale: Magma's awakened form is one of the cleanest pre-Mythical grinders. The burn DoT scales well into mid-game mob health pools, and the moves have generous hitboxes. PvP is workable thanks to the same DoT but lacks any real burst potential — you'll lose to anything that can rush you down.
pros: Awakened grinding is comparable to Light at a moderately higher cost
Burn DoT compounds with sword damage for steady chip pressure
Forgiving cooldowns — beginner-friendly rotation
cons: PvP ceiling caps at B — outpaced by every zoner
Awakening fragment grind is long relative to the payoff
Trading liquidity is weak post-rework

bestCombos.notes: Cyborg race for survivability during long grinding sessions.

fruits.name: Light
fruits.oneLineReason: Cheap, fast, and clears mobs all the way to 1500. Budget GOAT.
fruits.tierRationale: The budget grinder's best friend. Cheap to obtain, fast travel speed, and AOE moves that clear mob camps in seconds — Light is what most accounts use to grind from ~700 to ~1500 before swapping. PvP is mediocre by Mythical standards but viable against other Rare/Legendary opponents.
pros: Cheapest path to S-tier grinding — accessible early
Travel speed in elemental form saves dozens of hours over the playthrough
Forgiving — beginners can use Light effectively from day one
cons: PvP ceiling is hard-capped at B — outclassed by every Mythical
No awakening — what you see is what you get
Trading floor is low because supply is high

bestCombos.notes: Any race works; pick based on what your endgame fruit will be.

fruits.name: Phoenix
fruits.oneLineReason: Self-heal and permanent fly; easiest Mythical, weakest in PvP.
fruits.tierRationale: Self-heal makes Phoenix the most forgiving Mythical, which is exactly why it gets overpicked by new players and then sold. The fly mode is genuinely useful for grinding sea events and reaching out-of-bounds raid spawns, but PvP is well below the Mythical average — the heal is read easily and counter-pressured.
pros: Self-sustain in grinding makes long sessions painless
Permanent fly mode is a real quality-of-life upgrade for sea travel
Easiest Mythical to play — strong recommendation for first-time Mythical owners
cons: PvP ceiling is the lowest of any Mythical — hard-countered by AOE damage
Awakening fragment grind is long for what's effectively a quality-of-life fruit
Resale value drops once players realize the PvP ceiling

bestCombos.notes: Shark race underwater bonus stacks well with the sustain theme.

fruits.name: Rubber
fruits.oneLineReason: Gear-style speed buff; awakening makes it punch above its rarity.
fruits.tierRationale: Pre-awakening Rubber is a mid-tier joke pick; awakened it becomes a real PvP fruit thanks to lightning-fast Z chains and the bounce mechanic. Grinding suffers because the kit is single-target-focused. A surprise sleeper for players who want a cheap PvP option.
pros: Awakened Z chains hit faster than most Legendary moves
Immune to ranged stuns in awakened form — niche but real upside
Cheap Robux floor for a PvP-capable fruit
cons: Pre-awakening it's borderline unplayable
Grinding is C-tier; need a second fruit to level efficiently
Limited combo identity outside the Z chain

bestCombos.notes: Mink race amplifies the speed identity; this fruit is built around outpacing the opponent.

fruits.name: Sand
fruits.oneLineReason: Vacuum suction plus elemental immunity; a sleeper PvP pick.
fruits.tierRationale: Sand has a genuinely strong PvP suction kit — the V move pulls opponents into your sword range from across the screen. Elemental immunity helps against newer players. Grinding is the weak link: the kit lacks any large AOE and depends on melee follow-through.
pros: Suction pull is one of the better positioning tools at Uncommon rarity
Elemental immunity against weaker opponents
Cheap Beli cost — accessible mid-game pick
cons: Grinding is genuinely bad — single-target focus dominates the kit
Awakening adds little; this fruit doesn't scale to endgame
Counter-picked by Light, Rumble, and any zoner

bestCombos.notes: Cyborg race for the sustain Sand doesn't generate on its own.

fruits.name: Diamond
fruits.oneLineReason: Defensive Z stance; cheap PvP option for combo-focused builds.
fruits.tierRationale: Diamond's body-hardening Z makes it one of the more durable Uncommons in 1v1 PvP. The kit is built around tanking openers and counter-comboing, which works against impatient opponents. Grinding is poor: no AOE, no movement, no fun.
pros: Damage reduction stance gives genuine defensive identity at low rarity
Strong against low-skill aggressive players who can't bait the stance
Cheap to acquire and trade
cons: Grinding is painfully slow — single-target only
High-skill opponents bait the stance and punish on cooldown
No awakening; the ceiling is fixed

bestCombos.notes: Human race for the additional dodge i-frames pairs nicely with the stance pattern.

fruits.name: Ice
fruits.oneLineReason: Freeze on hit and an ice cage; a solid budget mid-game fruit.
fruits.tierRationale: Ice's freeze chance on Z gives it a stop-start pressure pattern that's frustrating for newer opponents. The cage move sets up real combo windows when it connects. Grinding works thanks to the AOE on F, though the cooldowns force breathers between mob waves. A decent generalist at Rare rarity.
pros: Freeze proc on hit creates free combo openings against weaker opponents
Ice cage is a genuine combo setup — rare for a Rare fruit
Travels at elemental speed; mob clears are reasonable
cons: Freeze chance is unreliable — feast-or-famine PvP
Counter-picked by Magma directly
No awakening; ceiling caps in mid-game

bestCombos.notes: Mink race for chase potential when the freeze procs.

fruits.name: Dark
fruits.oneLineReason: Pull-in plus a damage zone; an old-school combo opener.
fruits.tierRationale: Dark's pull-in on F is the cleanest opener at Uncommon rarity — connect it once and most opponents at this tier eat the full sword combo. The black hole zone keeps people honest. Grinding suffers from the lack of AOE damage in the kit beyond the single-target pulls.
pros: F pull-in is a textbook combo opener — easy to learn
Black hole zone controls space in 1v1 fights
Cheap and accessible mid-game
cons: Grinding is single-target — slow against mob groups
Counter-picked by Light's speed
No awakening keeps the ceiling locked

bestCombos.notes: Any race works; pick based on what you're planning to upgrade to next.

fruits.name: Flame
fruits.oneLineReason: Fast cooldowns and elemental travel; cheap early grinder.
fruits.tierRationale: Flame is the textbook 'first fruit after the starter' pick — short cooldowns, elemental immunity against weaker enemies, and decent travel speed. It's a stepping stone, not an endgame answer. PvP falls off fast once Legendary fruits enter the room.
pros: Short cooldowns make leveling Mastery quick
Elemental travel is a meaningful upgrade from melee-only
Cheap Beli cost — a sensible first purchase
cons: Outclassed by Magma directly in every dimension
Damage falls off in mid-game
Trading liquidity is poor because supply is endless

bestCombos.notes: Human race for the early-game ease; this fruit is a stepping stone anyway.

fruits.name: Paw
fruits.oneLineReason: Teleport-based pressure; unique kit, niche payoff.
fruits.tierRationale: Paw is the weird Mythical — teleport stamps, paw projectiles, and a unique kick-everything-away mechanic make it visually distinct, but the damage numbers don't match the rarity. Picked for novelty more than meta strength. Grinding is poor by Mythical standards.
pros: Unique kit — there's nothing else like it
Teleport stamps reach across the map for picking off runners
Trading value holds up due to rarity and visual appeal
cons: Damage scaling lags behind every other Mythical
Grinding is C-tier — the kit doesn't translate to mob clears
Steep learning curve for the teleport mechanic

bestCombos.notes: Mink race accelerates the teleport rotation; Ghoul for sustain.

fruits.name: Falcon
fruits.oneLineReason: Permanent flight at Uncommon price; mobility utility, weak damage.
fruits.tierRationale: Falcon is bought for the wings, not the moves. Permanent flight at Uncommon rarity is a real utility — sea travel and reaching out-of-bounds boss spawns become trivial. But damage and PvP are bottom-tier. Treat Falcon as a travel tool, not a real combat fruit.
pros: Cheap permanent flight — saves real grind time
Useful for trading and sea event logistics
Easy to obtain
cons: PvP is among the worst in the game
Damage scaling is awful past mid-game
Almost no one keeps it as their main fruit past Sea 2

bestCombos.notes: Race choice doesn't matter much — this is a utility pick.

fruits.name: Bomb
fruits.oneLineReason: Cheap starter; outgrown by hour ten of any account.
fruits.tierRationale: Bomb is fine for the first ten hours of an account. The damage is okay, the AOE is workable, and the Beli cost is low. But every fruit on this list outclasses it within a single tier of upgrades. Don't buy Bomb if you can afford anything better.
pros: Cheapest entry point for testing the Devil Fruit system
AOE moves help early Sea 1 mob clears
Easy to resell or eat through
cons: Outclassed by literally every Uncommon and above
PvP is non-existent past low levels
Trading value is rounded to zero

bestCombos.notes: Race choice irrelevant — replace this fruit before you finalize race.

howToObtain: Blox Fruit Dealer (Common roll, very frequent)

fruits.name: Spike
fruits.oneLineReason: Starter-tier; only useful if you found one in a sea spawn.
fruits.tierRationale: Spike is the textbook 'eat it because you found it' fruit. Slow projectiles, mediocre damage, no real combo identity. It's only on this list because new players keep asking if it's worth using. The answer is: only until you can buy literally anything else.
pros: Costs almost nothing in Beli
Common enough that you'll see one for free in a sea spawn
Acceptable as a 'first fruit before you commit Robux' option
cons: Slow projectiles are dodged trivially in PvP
Grinding pace is worse than melee-only
Zero trade value

bestCombos.notes: Stepping stone — don't optimize around this fruit.

fruits.name: Smoke
fruits.oneLineReason: Cheapest elemental immunity; outgrown almost immediately.
fruits.tierRationale: Smoke's only real selling point is being the cheapest Elemental — which means you get elemental travel and immunity to physical sword hits at a Common price. Damage and AOE are bottom of the barrel. Useful for Sea 1, outgrown by the time you reach the second island chain.
pros: Cheapest entry into the Elemental immunity mechanic
Travels slightly faster than running
Easy to find — Common rarity
cons: Damage is the worst of any Elemental
PvP ceiling stops at the lowest player level brackets
Replaced by Flame within a single tier

bestCombos.notes: Race choice irrelevant — Smoke is a transitional fruit only.

fruits.name: Spring
fruits.oneLineReason: Meme tier; the running joke of the Devil Fruit roster.
fruits.tierRationale: Spring is the universally-acknowledged worst fruit. The bounce moves don't combo into anything, the damage is negligible, and it can't even traverse water like Elementals can. Listed here only because new players keep finding one in a sea spawn and asking if it's salvageable. It isn't.
pros: Funny
Free if you find one in the wild
Eating it counts toward fruit collection achievements
cons: Worst PvP fruit by consensus
Worst grinding fruit by consensus
No redemption arc — replace immediately

bestCombos.notes: Eat it, log the achievement, replace it with literally any Uncommon.
